fatal_errors: The proposed feed contains W, Mo, Ta, and Nb but omits V, so it does not reconstruct the target WNbMoTaV refractory high-entropy alloy.
The claimed Ti(Al,Cu)2-like structural mediator is chemically unsupported because no Cu-containing component is specified; it is imported from evidence about a different Ti-Al-Cu-Ni coating system.
Preservation of ductility and tensile properties is asserted but neither supported by the cited WMoTaNb evidence nor measured in the proposed experiment.
explanation: The hypothesis correctly identifies laser cladding of a refractory multicomponent coating as a route to improve TC4 hardness and sliding-wear resistance, and its lattice-distortion, solid-solution-strengthening, stress-buffering, and dislocation-obstruction arguments partially agree with the target mechanism. However, it misses the WNbMoTaV composition, spherical-powder preparation, 2 mm preset layer, controlled 3.1–3.9 kW power study, optimum near 3.5 kW, BCC-plus-Ti-rich structure, grain refinement, dilution, Marangoni transport, and tribo-oxide contribution. Its broad 10–30 N ambient test conditions do not reconstruct the specified 20 N Si3N4 reciprocating test or hardness protocol. The predicted greater-than-twofold hardness increase slightly overstates the target maximum of 1.97 times, and no nonmonotonic power dependence is predicted. The experiment has a useful untreated control and relevant measurements, but the coating formulation and cladding parameters are insufficiently defined, and its conjunctive falsification rule is weak because failure of either promised performance endpoint should be sufficient. The evidence is mainly analogical: WMoTaNb on 316L and Ti-Al-Cu-Ni on TC4 do not directly validate the proposed phase constitution or preservation of TC4 ductility.
